// Found in envelope\n205\t                }\n206\t            }\n207\t            // Fallback to payload (using path without ^)\n208\t            extract_field(payload, envelope_path)\n209\t        } payload only\n215\t        extract_field(payload, path)\n216\t    }\n217\t}\n218\t\n219\t/// Extract a string field from either envelope or payload based on path prefix\n220\t///\n221\t/// Wrapper around `extract_with_envelope` that converts the raw `Value` to a string,\n222\t/// following the same coercion rules as `extract_string` (String, Number, Bool, Null).\n223\tpub fn extract_string_with_envelope(\n224\t    path: &str,\n225\t    payload: &Value,\n226\t    envelope: Option<&Value>,\n227\t) -> Option<String> {\n228\t    let value = extract_with_envelope(path, payload, envelope)?;\n229\t    match value {\n230\t        Value::String(s) => Some(s),\n231\t        Value::Number(n) => Some(n.to_string()),\n232\t        Value::Bool(b) => Some(b.to_string()),\n233\t        Value::Null => Some(String::new()),\n234\t        Value::Array(arr) => {\n235\t            // Handle content arrays (e.g., Claude Code format with text blocks and tool calls)\n236\t            // Extract text from all text blocks in the array\n237\t            let text_parts: Vec<String> = arr\n238\t                .iter()\n239\t                .filter_map(|item| {\n240\t                    if let Some(obj) = item.as_object() {\n241\t                        // Check for text blocks: {\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"...\"}\n242\t                        if obj.get(\"type\").and_then(|t| t.as_str()) == Some(\"text\") {\n243\t                            return obj\n244\t                                .get(\"text\")\n245\t                                .and_then(|t| t.as_str())\n246\t                                .map(|s| s.to_string());\n247\t                        }\n248\t                    }\n249\t                    None\n250\t                })\n251\t                .collect();\n252\t            if text_parts.is_empty() {\n253\t                None\n254\t            } else {\n255\t                Some(text_parts.join(\" \"))\n256\t            }\n257\t        }\n258\t        _ => None,\n259\t    }\n260\t}\n261\t\n262\t/// Parse a timestamp from either envelope or payload based on path prefix\n263\t///\n264\t/// Wrapper around `extract_string_with_envelope` that parses the extracted string\n265\t/// as a timestamp. Supports ISO 8601, Unix epoch (seconds/milliseconds), and\n266\t/// UTC-naive formats.\n267\tpub fn parse_timestamp_with_envelope(\n268\t    path: &str,\n269\t    payload: &Value,\n270\t    envelope: Option<&Value>,\n271\t) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>> {\n272\t    let ts_str = extract_string_with_envelope(path, payload, envelope)\n273\t        .ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\"Field '{}' not found\", path)))?;\n274\t\n275\t    // Try ISO 8601 first\n276\t    if let Ok(dt) = DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&ts_str) {\n277\t        return Ok(dt.with_timezone(&Utc));\n278\t    }\n279\t\n280\t    // Try parsing as Unix epoch (seconds)\n281\t    if let Ok(seconds) = ts_str.parse::<i64>() {\n282\t        let ts = if seconds > 1_000_000_000_000 {\n283\t            // Milliseconds\n284\t            DateTime::from_timestamp_millis(seconds)\n285\t        } else {\n286\t            // Seconds\n287\t            DateTime::from_timestamp(seconds, 0)\n288\t        };\n289\t        return ts.ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(\"Invalid timestamp\".to_string()));\n290\t    }\n291\t\n292\t    // Try parsing without timezone (assume UTC)\n293\t    if let Ok(dt) = ts_str.parse::<DateTime<Utc>>() {\n294\t        return Ok(dt);\n295\t    }\n296\t\n297\t    Err(AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\n298\t        \"Cannot parse timestamp: {}\",\n299\t        ts_str\n300\t    )))\n301\t}\n302\t\n303\t/// Base trait for all format parsers\n304\tpub trait FormatParser {\n305\t    /// Parse events from the source\n306\t    fn parse(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<Event>>;\n307\t\n308\t    /// Parse events from the source, starting from a given byte offset for incremental parsing.\n309\t    ///\n310\t    /// For formats that support incremental parsing (JSONL, append-only logs), this allows\n311\t    /// the parser to skip already-processed content and only parse new data.\n312\t    ///\n313\t    /// # Arguments\n314\t    ///\n315\t    /// * `source_path` - Path to the source file\n316\t    /// * `plugin` - Plugin configuration for this source\n317\t    /// * `start_offset` - Byte offset to start reading from (0 for full parse)\n318\t    ///\n319\t    /// # Returns\n320\t    ///\n321\t    /// - `Ok(events)` - Vector of parsed events\n322\t    /// - `Err(_)` - Parse error (check `is_skippable()` for non-fatal errors)\n323\t    fn parse_incremental(\n324\t        &self,\n325\t        source_path: &Path,\n326\t        plugin: &Plugin,\n327\t        start_offset: u64,\n328\t    ) -> Result<Vec<Event>> {\n329\t        // Default implementation falls back to full parse\n330\t        let _ = start_offset; // Suppress unused warning\n331\t        self.parse(source_path, plugin)\n332\t    }\n333\t\n334\t    /// Detect session boundaries in the source\n335\t    fn detect_sessions(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<SessionInfo>>;\n336\t}\n337\t\n338\t/// Information about a detected session\n339\t#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\n340\t#[allow(dead_code)]\n341\tpub struct SessionInfo {\n342\t    pub session_id: String,\n343\t    pub start_offset: u64,\n344\t    pub end_offset: u64,\n345\t    pub metadata: Option<Value>,\n346\t    /// Parent session ID (populated for subagent sessions where this session\n347\t    /// is a child of another session)\n348\t    pub parent_session_id: Option<String>,\n349\t}\n350\t\n351\t#[cfg(test)]\n352\tmod tests {\n353\t    use super::*;\n354\t    use serde_json::json;\n355\t\n356\t    #[test]\n357\t    fn usize,\n}\n\nimpl ParseContext {\n    pub fn new(session_id: String, source_agent: String, source_file: String) -> Self {\n        ParseContext {\n            session_id,\n            source_agent,\n            source_file,\n            project: None,\n            model: None,\n            line_number: 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    pub fn with_project(mut self, project: Option<String>) -> Self {\n        self.project = project;\n        self\n    }\n\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    pub fn with_model(mut self, model: Option<String>) -> Self {\n        self.model = model;\n        self\n    }\n\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    pub fn increment_line(&mut self) {\n        self.line_number += 1;\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if a field name has a caret prefix (^)\n///\n/// Returns true if the field name starts with `^`, false otherwise.\n/// Handles empty strings gracefully (returns false).\n///\n/// # Examples\n/// ```\n/// use agentscribe::parser::has_caret_prefix;\n///\n/// assert!(has_caret_prefix(\"^foo\"));\n/// assert!(!has_caret_prefix(\"foo\"));\n/// assert!(!has_caret_prefix(\"bar^baz\"));\n/// assert!(!has_caret_prefix(\"\"));\n/// ```\npub fn has_caret_prefix(field_name: &str) -> bool {\n    field_name.starts_with('^')\n}\n\n/// Extract a nested field from JSON using dot notation\npub fn extract_field(value: &Value, path: &str) -> Option<Value> {\n    if path.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    let mut current = value;\n    for part in path.split('.') {\n        // Handle array indexing like parts[0]\n        if let Some(bracket_pos) = part.find('[') {\n            let key = &part[..bracket_pos];\n            let index_str = &part[bracket_pos + 1..part.len() - 1];\n            let index: usize = index_str.parse().ok()?;\n\n            current = current.get(key)?.get(index)?;\n        } else {\n            current = current.get(part)?;\n        }\n    }\n    Some(current.clone())\n}\n\n/// Extract a string field from JSON\npub fn extract_string(value: &Value, path: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    let field = extract_field(value, path)?;\n    match field {\n        Value::String(s) => Some(s),\n        Value::Number(n) => Some(n.to_string()),\n        Value::Bool(b) => Some(b.to_string()),\n        Value::Null => Some(String::new()),\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parse timestamp from various formats\npub fn parse_timestamp(value: &Value, path: &str) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>> {\n    let ts_str = extract_string(value, path)\n        .ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\"Field '{}' not found\", path)))?;\n\n    // Try ISO 8601 first\n    if let Ok(dt) = DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&ts_str) {\n        return Ok(dt.with_timezone(&Utc));\n    }\n\n    // Try parsing as Unix epoch (seconds)\n    if let Ok(seconds) = ts_str.parse::<i64>() {\n        let ts = if seconds > 1_000_000_000_000 {\n            // Milliseconds\n            DateTime::from_timestamp_millis(seconds)\n        } else {\n            // Seconds\n            DateTime::from_timestamp(seconds, 0)\n        };\n        return ts.ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(\"Invalid timestamp\".to_string()));\n    }\n\n    // Try parsing without timezone (assume UTC)\n    if let Ok(dt) = ts_str.parse::<DateTime<Utc>>() {\n        return Ok(dt);\n    }\n\n    Err(AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\n        \"Cannot parse timestamp: {}\",\n        ts_str\n    )))\n}\n\n/// Extract a field from either envelope or payload based on path prefix\n///\n/// **Envelope-first with payload fallback for caret-prefixed paths:**\n/// - If path starts with `^`, try envelope first (remove `^` prefix)\n/// - If envelope is None OR field not found in envelope, fallback to payload\n/// - Otherwise, extract from payload only\n///\n/// **Resolution order for `^field`:**\n/// 1. Try `envelope.field` (if envelope exists)\n/// 2. Fallback to `payload.field` (if envelope missing or field not found)\n/// 3. Return None (if both fail)\n///\n/// **Resolution order for `field` (no caret):**\n/// - Extract from `payload.field` only\n///\n/// Supports dot notation for nested fields (e.g., `^outer.ts` or `user.role`)\n/// and array indexing (e.g., `items[0].name`).\npub fn extract_with_envelope(\n    path: &str,\n    payload: &Value,\n    envelope: Option<&Value>,\n) -> Option<Value> {\n    if has_caret_prefix(path) {\n        // Strip the caret prefix\n        if let Some(envelope_path) = path.strip_prefix('^') {\n            // Try envelope first\n            if let Some(env) = envelope {\n                if let Some(value) = extract_field(env, envelope_path) {\n                    return Some(value); // Found in envelope\n                }\n            }\n            // Fallback to payload (using path without ^)\n            extract_field(payload, envelope_path)\n        } else {\n            // Should not happen due to starts_with check, but handle defensively\n            None\n        }\n    } else {\n        // No caret prefix - extract from payload only\n        extract_field(payload, path)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Extract a string field from either envelope or payload based on path prefix\n///\n/// Wrapper around `extract_with_envelope` that converts the raw `Value` to a string,\n/// following the same coercion rules as `extract_string` (String, Number, Bool, Null).\npub fn extract_string_with_envelope(\n    path: &str,\n    payload: &Value,\n    envelope: Option<&Value>,\n) -> Option<String> {\n    let value = extract_with_envelope(path, payload, envelope)?;\n    match value {\n        Value::String(s) => Some(s),\n        Value::Number(n) => Some(n.to_string()),\n        Value::Bool(b) => Some(b.to_string()),\n        Value::Null => Some(String::new()),\n        Value::Array(arr) => {\n            // Handle content arrays (e.g., Claude Code format with text blocks and tool calls)\n            // Extract text from all text blocks in the array\n            let text_parts: Vec<String> = arr\n                .iter()\n                .filter_map(|item| {\n                    if let Some(obj) = item.as_object() {\n                        // Check for text blocks: {\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"...\"}\n                        if obj.get(\"type\").and_then(|t| t.as_str()) == Some(\"text\") {\n                            return obj\n                                .get(\"text\")\n                                .and_then(|t| t.as_str())\n                                .map(|s| s.to_string());\n                        }\n                    }\n                    None\n                })\n                .collect();\n            if text_parts.is_empty() {\n                None\n            } else {\n                Some(text_parts.join(\" \"))\n            }\n        }\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parse a timestamp from either envelope or payload based on path prefix\n///\n/// Wrapper around `extract_string_with_envelope` that parses the extracted string\n/// as a timestamp. Supports ISO 8601, Unix epoch (seconds/milliseconds), and\n/// UTC-naive formats.\npub fn parse_timestamp_with_envelope(\n    path: &str,\n    payload: &Value,\n    envelope: Option<&Value>,\n) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>> {\n    let ts_str = extract_string_with_envelope(path, payload, envelope)\n        .ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\"Field '{}' not found\", path)))?;\n\n    // Try ISO 8601 first\n    if let Ok(dt) = DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&ts_str) {\n        return Ok(dt.with_timezone(&Utc));\n    }\n\n    // Try parsing as Unix epoch (seconds)\n    if let Ok(seconds) = ts_str.parse::<i64>() {\n        let ts = if seconds > 1_000_000_000_000 {\n            // Milliseconds\n            DateTime::from_timestamp_millis(seconds)\n        } else {\n            // Seconds\n            DateTime::from_timestamp(seconds, 0)\n        };\n        return ts.ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(\"Invalid timestamp\".to_string()));\n    }\n\n    // Try parsing without timezone (assume UTC)\n    if let Ok(dt) = ts_str.parse::<DateTime<Utc>>() {\n        return Ok(dt);\n    }\n\n    Err(AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\n        \"Cannot parse timestamp: {}\",\n        ts_str\n    )))\n}\n\n/// Base trait for all format parsers\npub trait FormatParser {\n    /// Parse events from the source\n    fn parse(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<Event>>;\n\n    /// Parse events from the source, starting from a given byte offset for incremental parsing.\n    ///\n    /// For formats that support incremental parsing (JSONL, append-only logs), this allows\n    /// the parser to skip already-processed content and only parse new data.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `source_path` - Path to the source file\n    /// * `plugin` - Plugin configuration for this source\n    /// * `start_offset` - Byte offset to start reading from (0 for full parse)\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    ///\n    /// - `Ok(events)` - Vector of parsed events\n    /// - `Err(_)` - Parse error (check `is_skippable()` for non-fatal errors)\n    fn parse_incremental(\n        &self,\n        source_path: &Path,\n        plugin: &Plugin,\n        start_offset: u64,\n    ) -> Result<Vec<Event>> {\n        // Default implementation falls back to full parse\n        let _ = start_offset; // Suppress unused warning\n        self.parse(source_path, plugin)\n    }\n\n    /// Detect session boundaries in the source\n    fn detect_sessions(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<SessionInfo>>;\n}\n\n/// Information about a detected session\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\n#[allow(dead_code)]\npub struct SessionInfo {\n    pub session_id: String,\n    pub start_offset: u64,\n    pub end_offset: u64,\n    pub metadata: Option<Value>,\n    /// Parent session ID (populated for subagent sessions where this session\n    /// is a child of another session)\n    pub parent_session_id: Option<String>,\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use serde_json::json;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_extract_field_simple() {\n        let value = json!({\"name\": \"test\", {\n        let now = Utc::now();\n        let scan_threshold = now - Duration::hours(CONFIG_SCAN_WINDOW_HOURS);\n\n        // Discover projects from session manifests\n
